creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Muster now writes the config its daemon reads - `~/.muster/state/herdr.toml`, named to the
daemon with `HERDR_CONFIG_PATH` - so `scrollback_bytes` and `[shell]` decide what a local pane
runs and the pinned daemon's update checks stay off. A pane on the devenv gets none of that.
An ssh endpoint attaches to whatever herdr is installed over there, so there is no daemon of
Muster's to configure and no file of Muster's on that machine to configure it with.

The result is a window whose two halves disagree about settings the person wrote once. A
scrollback depth or a shell named in `~/.muster/config.toml` applies to the panes on this
machine and silently not to the ones beside them, which is the sort of difference nobody
reports as a bug because it reads as the remote machine simply being different.

**Per-daemon is the right shape rather than a compromise**, and this is the second reason for
it: two machines can want different answers - a devenv's shell is not a laptop's - so a single
Muster-wide daemon config would have to pretend otherwise. What is missing is the delivery,
not the model.

Nothing new is needed to deliver it. `crates/muster-ssh` already holds an ssh master per
remote daemon and `Tunnel::control_path()` is already threaded to the shell, so the file rides
the connection that is already open - the same trick `muster-bridge` uses to run a command on
the far side. The wrinkle is ordering: the file has to land before the daemon reads it, and
today Muster does not start the remote daemon at all.

**Which makes this land naturally with a_28QlRpvKj** ("Put our own daemon on the devenv"),
rather than before it. Once Muster starts the remote daemon it also decides when, and "write
the config, then start it" is the same sequence the local path already has. Doing it first
would mean asking a daemon somebody else started to re-read a config it was not started with,
which reaches only its update checks and leaves what a pane runs where it was.
title: 🛰️ A devenv pane runs the settings a laptop pane does
